processes: Starting protein breakdown with acid and enzymes
Passing chyme to the small intestine
plainLanguageExplanation: The stomach is a J-shaped muscular bag at the top of the abdomen. When food arrives from the esophagus, the stomach stretches and churns it with strong muscles, mixing it with gastric juices - acid and enzymes that start breaking down the food, especially proteins. The acid also kills many germs that come in with food. After a few hours, the food has become a soupy mixture called chyme, which moves into the small intestine. The stomach has a thick lining with special cells that make the acid and enzymes, and a layer of mucus protects the stomach wall from digesting itself.

whyItMatters: The stomach is where digestion really kicks in - it starts breaking down proteins and killing germs. Understanding it explains heartburn, why you feel full after a meal, and how digestion begins.
didYouKnow: The stomach can stretch to hold about 1-1.5 liters of food and drink, then shrink back down when it is empty.
